updates.statement: Most of the early wall-time reduction came from cutting the epochs needed to reach 75%, through the backbone, optimizer and averaging choices: the airbench96 port, Muon, Lookahead and wd ×0.5. Resizing, compile, averaging, backward truncation (whitening at 6%, group 1 at 75%, group 2 at 90%) and early 20 px trims bring the tip to E061: 5.02 s, with a population mean of ~0.7532 (40 fresh draws on seeds 33–52) and seeds 0–2 at 0.7534. The organizer's ResNet9 baseline (59.30 s) comes from forks, was never run here, and is external and unverified. The ~12x figure is indicative only. No accuracy-per-epoch booster has gained ≥0.25 pp since E016. With H4.4 refuted, the post-keep negatives are probably real effects of about −0.2 to −0.27 pp, not seed-set artefacts: E022 (wd ×0.25), E025 (harder pull), E030 (longer free runs) and E032 (late LS removal). The copied airbench scalars therefore sit near a local optimum. Muon vs SGD is now tested: E062 cost −3.0 pp, though only one untuned SGD configuration was tried (H1.2). Still untested: Muon momentum and lr on the current tip (N1.1), batch size (H5), plain EMA and LS 0.1. Coarse labels have a strong literature counter-prior (H1.8).
updates.reason: Refreshed to the E061 tip and the fresh-seed population. Removed the 'flat fits as well as harmful' hedges, which relied on H4.4, now contradicted by E057. Moved Muon vs SGD to tested (E062). Labelled the baseline ratio as external.

updates.statement: Muon (Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized Nesterov momentum) on the conv filters, with SGD on BatchNorm biases and the head, reaches 75% on CIFAR-100 in far fewer steps than Nesterov SGD in this recipe. E006: +0.66 pp at ~10 epochs, confounded with batch and RNG. E062: replacing Muon with SGD on the 226-step tip cost −3.0 pp at −5.6% time. Caveats: E062 tested one SGD configuration (momentum 0.85, airbench lr scaled linearly to batch 2000). Its seed spread (sd ~0.05 pp vs the usual 0.2–0.3) suggests a systematic mis-scaling may inflate the gap (N2). PR #3 reports tuned SGD beating Muon on airbench96 at 8.5 epochs, which is not refuted.
updates.reason: E062 confirms H1.2.2's directional prediction (≥0.3 pp loss) by 10x. It was mislabelled 'refutes' only because the experiment's pre-registered range missed. The confidence is held below 0.7 because only one untuned SGD point was tried and the magnitude looks partly like a scaling artefact.

E062+ (re-logged; it was mislogged E062-). The prediction was a drop of ≥0.3 pp; the drop was 3.0 pp, so the hypothesis is confirmed. The time prediction (~2%) was too small: the real saving was 5.6%, and the excess is examined in N3. The verdict logic must separate an 'experiment range missed' from the 'hypothesis direction'.

updates.statement: In short CIFAR-100 runs, end-of-run averaging is a first-order lever: Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp at E005, with every seed gaining. The airbench Lookahead settings (every 5 steps, cubic ramp) and LS 0.3 throughout look like a local optimum. A harder pull (E025, −0.27 pp), longer free runs (E030, −0.24 pp) and dropping LS late (E032, −0.23 pp) are probably real ~0.2 pp harms. They are no longer explained away as seed-set bias, because E057 shows rebuilds re-draw per-seed outcomes. With averaging on, the final-LR floor does not matter (E009, C0021). Recomputing BN statistics of the averaged weights adds nothing (E044, paired). Plain EMA (H1.3.5) is untested, and external data (EMA ≈ SWA ≈ Lookahead on CIFAR-100) suggest its effect is small.
updates.reason: The H4.4 hedge was rolled back after E057 and E049's 0.05 pp fresh-seed shift. Search (Switch-EMA and Lookahead tables) supports averaging variants being roughly equivalent.
Search: on CIFAR-100, EMA (78.55) ≈ SWA (78.69), and Lookahead ≥ SWA at the end of training, so a ≥0.15 pp swing is unlikely. Kept open at low priority.

Search: the airbench paper measures alternating flip, without TTA, as worth a 15% effective epoch speedup at 10 epochs and 27% at 20. With TTA banned, it must be kept, and trims must preserve the parity alternation. This rests on literature, not a loop test, so confidence is held at 0.7. The committee was split 2/2; this evidence resolves the split.

updates.statement: The optimizer and regularization settings copied from CIFAR-10 airbench may not be optimal for short CIFAR-100 runs. Measured on held-out seeds: wd ×0.5 helps (E016, +0.24 pp); wd ×0.25 on the SGD groups probably hurts (E022, −0.24 pp, now read as real). E013 (LS 0.2 vs 0.3), E014 (Muon lr ×1.5) and E009 (LR floor) were 'not detected at 3-seed power'. E062 makes Muon load-bearing, yet Muon momentum 0.6 has never been varied, and the Muon lr was tested once, at 3 seeds. Whether further regularizer changes (LS 0.1, jitter, ghost BN) can pay depends on whether the recipe under-fits (N1.2.1), which has never been measured.
updates.reason: Folded in E062's load-bearing finding and the review's under- vs over-fitting gap, and restored E022 as a probable real harm.

The search finds long-run CIFAR-100 LS optima of 0.02–0.1, but the loop's short-run evidence (E013 flat 0.2–0.3; E032 late LS removal −0.23 pp) transfers against it. The committee split refuted 2 / unknown 2. Run it only if N1.2.1 shows the recipe is not under-fitting.

updates.statement: On the E061 tip, raising the Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5), with everything else unchanged, raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds (60 draws) by at least 0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds at unchanged time. This follows E014's +0.09 pp (3 seeds) on the higher-wd base. 0.12 pp is about what a +0.1 s top-up buys at the measured dial.
updates.reason: Re-based from the stale E017 tip onto E061 with the 60-draw rule. This is a direct child-level test of N1.1, prioritised now that E062 shows Muon is load-bearing.

The committee unanimously expects this to be refuted. The search finds no per-technique ablation for Hiverge's jitter. It is now conditional on N1.2.1: run it only if train accuracy is near saturation.
The committee unanimously expects this to be refuted, and E016/E022 suggest more regularization does not help. Parked behind the N1.2.1 diagnostic.

Search: HAF (ECCV 2022) finds that hierarchy-aware soft labels and HXE on CIFAR-100 cost 4.7–9.9 pp of top-1, and the best method only ties cross-entropy. That is a strong counter-prior. The precondition (RULES.md permission) is still unread.

The HAF and Bertinetto counter-prior predicts a neutral-to-negative result. The milder mix (half of LS 0.3 spread over the 4 same-superclass classes) is the only reason not to retire it. Check RULES.md first.

updates.statement: Removing kernel-launch and Python overhead speeds up each step without changing the math. Compile plus a fused optimizer gave −14% (E004). After that the step is GPU-bound: CUDA graphs gave −0.9% (E015), graph-break removal −0.5% (E017), and GPU idle is 2.8% (E047). Rebuild variance comes from autotune kernel reselection and is not removed by dropping cudagraphs (E050). One open residue: E062's SGD swap saved 0.28 s per trial, while Newton-Schulz GPU time is only ~0.18 s (0.8 ms × 226 steps). The ~0.1 s gap may be per-call overhead of the separate per-group Muon calls (N3).
updates.reason: Added the E062 time counterexample, which no member predicted, as a candidate residual overhead.

updates.statement: Progressive resizing is a near-linear time dial for tile-friendly sizes (about 0.51/0.71/0.89 s per epoch at 24/28/32 px, E012). The 28 and 32 px phases carry accuracy: dropping the 28 px phase cost −0.68 pp (E018), and shrinking the 32 px tail to 20% cost −0.97 pp (E011, confounded). Early low resolution is cheap: E026 −0.15 pp, E033 0.00 pp. The 24 px bridge, however, probably carries real accuracy: E040 read −0.28 pp, and this is no longer discounted as seed bias. Removing early 20 px steps was nearly free on fresh seeds (E061: −0.02 ± 0.06 pp). Candidate mechanisms for the late-phase loss remain unseparated: (a) low resolution at peak LR; (b) a FixRes/BN shift at the final jump; (c) too little 32 px fine-tuning. H2.3.5 and the re-based H2.3.7 would discriminate them.
updates.reason: E040 reinterpreted after H4.4 was refuted; added E061. H2.3.8 retired as superseded.

updates.statement: The 32 px share carries accuracy (mechanism c). On the E061 tip, move the 28→32 px switch from 70% to 65% of steps: the 28 px phase is shortened and the 32 px phase lengthened, while the step count, the group-1 freeze at 75% and all other schedules stay the same. This costs about +7.5 ms × ~11 steps ≈ +0.08 s. Prediction: the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds rises by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds. That beats the ~0.77 s/pp dial (break-even ~0.10 pp).
updates.reason: Re-based on E061. The old version (moving 10% of steps out of 24 px) would empty the 24 px bridge that E040 showed carries accuracy. The new version is a cheap margin booster and also tests mechanism (c).
Superseded: this is E040's schedule, already run (−0.28 pp). With H4.4 refuted, that reading is no longer attributed to seed bias, and the hypothesis was phrased against stale seeds 13–32.

The committee unanimously expects this to be refuted. E047 shows the convs run at 200–270 TF/s, so MAC cuts translate to time only at about the dial's rate. E051 shows the stem's structure is load-bearing (−1.1 pp). There is no mechanism for a discount.

updates.statement: Truncating the backward pass saves far more than the truncated FLOP share (H6.6), but only on layers that have finished learning. Free cases: the whitening bias after 6% (E060), and group 1 plus whitening over the last 25% (E028, E034). Group 2 over the last 10% costs about one dial-rate quantity (E046, E049). Costly cases: stem freeze from 60% (E037, −0.56 pp); from 71% (E055, −0.29 pp); conv1-only from 60% (E042, −0.21 pp); intermittent stem backward (E054, −0.48 pp, implementation unverified); group 2 from 85% (E053, −0.24 pp). Caveat: every freeze-dose test moved the anneal end together with the detach point. So E037/E055/E053 are composites of 'lost late steps' and a 'compressed group LR decay over the whole run', and they do not establish a sharp knee at 75% (N5, H2.6.6). The 75% point itself was judged 'free' on 10 seeds (E028, SE ~0.12 pp), so it may cost 0.1–0.2 pp now (N4).

Not run, and now more important: together with N5 it separates anneal compression from lost late steps, which confounds every freeze-dose reading (E037, E053, E055).

updates.statement: The whitening bias finishes learning far earlier than 20% of steps (Hiverge ~2.6%, airbench96 6.7%). On the E049 tip, moving the whitening detach (with its LR annealed to 0) from 20% to 6% of steps cuts mean time by 0.3–0.7% and loses no more than 0.05 pp on fresh seeds 33–52 against E049 on the same seeds. Judge time on per-step CUDA-event timing. Also verify by code read that E061 (376f231) carries the 6% detach: its description says 'on the E049 tip'.
updates.reason: E060: the accuracy clause was met (+0.09 pp, ~1.2σ, on 20 draws). The time clause is unverified: −0.4% wall time sits inside the 5.19–5.22 s build spread, and the promised per-step CUDA-event timing was not reported. Not closed on a within-noise result.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy margin on the local bar. The tip is E061 (5.02 s), with a population mean of ~0.7532 (40 fresh draws). Seeds 0–2 vary across builds with SD ~0.17 pp around the population mean (E049: 7 builds, mean 0.7535 vs population 0.7534), so E061 passes the local 0.753 bar only ~50% of the time per build. The official 40-seed 0.75 bar is safe for any candidate with a population of ≥~0.752 (E058). Passing locally with ≥80% probability needs a population of ≥~0.7545. The job is therefore buying margin with properly powered, near-time-neutral boosters, not loosening the gate. Decision rule: any keep whose effect is <0.2 pp needs ≥3 builds × 20 fresh seeds per arm (SE of the difference ≈0.055 pp), and any time claim under 1% needs per-step CUDA-event timing.
updates.reason: Refreshed to E061 and the E057/E058 measurements. The old claim that E052/E053 were 'discarded by a gate never connected to the official bar' is superseded by E058: the official gate passed, and the local bar binds.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise has three established parts and one suspect part. (a) Rebuild: a built artifact is deterministic (E050), but every rebuild re-draws each seed's outcome. Per-seed results are uncorrelated across builds (r ≈ −0.14 to 0.12, E057), so the rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean is ≲0.06 pp; 3 builds bound it but cannot estimate it. (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed SD is 0.15–0.35 pp, and the seeds 0–2 mean SD across builds is ~0.17 pp. (c) Suspect seed-1 effect: in a blind recount over post-E049 builds (E049–E062, 15 runs), seed 1 was the lowest of seeds 0–2 in 9, against a base rate of 5 (p≈0.03). That is suggestive but sits uneasily with (a). It has no practical effect on the gate, because the seeds 0–2 build mean matches the population (0.7535 vs 0.7534). (d) Selection: only the kept tip's own recorded value is biased, by ~0.05 pp (E049; N6).
updates.reason: Updated after E057: H4.5 is refuted, and seed sets have no persistent identity. Added a blind seed-1 recount from the logged per-seed values, as the review requested.

E057: per-seed differences between builds are uncorrelated (r −0.14 to 0.12), and the three 20-seed means agree within an SD of 0.013 pp. The 0.08–0.2 pp correlated build component is not present. Three builds bound σ_build at ≲0.06 pp; use that upper bound, not 0, in the gate.

updates.statement: Local SXM4 results transfer to the PCIe judge only partly. The PCIe card has a 300 W cap, ~5% less bandwidth and the same fp16 peak, so judged absolute times should come in ~5–10% higher, while the lever ranking mostly holds. The accuracy risk on the judge is small: the judge's own build re-draws per-seed outcomes, but the rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean is ≲0.06 pp (E057), and a 40-seed mean is more stable still. For any candidate with a fresh population of ≥0.752, P(official ≥0.75) is ≥0.95.
updates.reason: Updated with E057's build-robustness of multi-seed means. It replaces the earlier claim that kernel reselection could move the judged mean by up to 0.35 pp, which applies only to 3-seed means.

updates.statement: The keep gate is derived from P(official 40-seed mean ≥0.75 on the judge's build) and P(local 3-seed mean ≥0.753), and is frozen (E058). Inputs: the fresh-seed population mean, SE20, SD_seed²/40, σ_build ≤0.06 pp (upper bound) and a 0.05 pp judge-drift term. The official clause is easy (σ_tot ~0.09 pp; E052 at a population of 0.7524 passed twice). The local clause binds: with a seeds 0–2 build SD of ~0.17 pp, a population of ~0.7535 passes ~50% of the time and ~0.7545 passes ~80%. So the gate does not over-price official margin, but local margin must be bought.
updates.reason: E058 implemented the gate. E052 passed the official clause but failed its single local build, which shows the local bar is the binding term.
E058: E052 met all three clauses (population 0.7524 ≥0.751; P(official) ≥0.9; deficit vs E049 ≈0.10 ≤0.15 pp). E053 was not run, so the 'both' clause is untested.

updates.statement: At a fixed number of data passes, the optimizer step count (batch size) sets accuracy independently of the epoch count. Batch 2000 has not moved since E006. Time side: E047 shows time is ~95% proportional to samples processed, so batch changes alter time only through per-step overhead (≲1–3%). Batch is therefore mainly an accuracy axis. A smaller batch is a candidate booster if its accuracy gain beats the dial; a larger batch saves at most a few percent. Signals point both ways: E045 (more early steps, +0.135 pp, ~1.7σ) and Hiverge's 1536 favour smaller batches; Muon critical-batch theory (6x larger b* at β=0.6 than at 0.95) favours larger ones.
updates.reason: The search bounds the time side (E047 and Seesaw's step-bound mechanism), which reframes batch as an accuracy lever.

updates.statement: On the E061 tip, at the same true epoch count, lowering the batch from 2000 to 1600 (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr per step unchanged, every schedule kept as a data-progress fraction, graphs recaptured) raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds, at ≤+2.5% time. That rate (≤~1 s/pp) would match or beat the dial.
updates.reason: Re-based on E061 with the 60-draw rule and a milder batch (the review's 1600). The committee unanimously expected the 1500/≥0.2 pp version to be refuted, so the threshold was lowered to the dial's break-even. Muon critical-batch theory argues against it, so the prior stays low.

Search: Seesaw's saving comes from fewer sequential steps, which only matters when steps are overhead-bound. Here per-sample cost is fixed (E047), so late batch growth saves <1% at best, and it is untested on vision.
The time ceiling (≤1–3% from per-step overhead, E047) makes the ≥1.5% clause tight. Muon critical-batch theory supports the accuracy clause. Re-base on E061 with 60 draws if run.

Weakened. E061 found removing 12 early 20 px steps nearly free (−0.02 pp on fresh seeds), which contradicts 'removing steps costs about a uniform trim' for early steps; E041's counter-reading was on 10 seeds. E045's +0.135 pp is ~1.7σ. The committee unanimously supports it, but the fresh-seed data do not.

E056 supports the memory-bound account: ReLU's mask-only backward cut 4.8% of time, beyond the forecasts, which explains that counterexample. E043 and E047 (convs at 200–270 TF/s, fused elementwise 27%) and E046 (counterexample explained via H6.6) also support it. All four committee members vote supported.

updates.statement: The memory-bound fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels (27% of a 32 px step, E043) can be shrunk only by moving fewer bytes, because Inductor cannot fold training-mode BN into a conv epilogue. Activation branch: only mask-based activations (ReLU-like) save backward bytes, since GELU, SiLU and tanh-GELU all save the full fp16 input. ReLU's saving (−4.8%) costs 0.54 pp (E056), so the activation route closes unless erf compute, not bytes, is part of GELU's cost (N9). Remaining routes are BN statistics on a subset (H6.5.2) and split-reduction fixes (H6.5.3).
updates.reason: Search (Inverted Activations and PyTorch autograd behaviour) plus E056.
E056-: −4.8% time (the ≥3% clause was met) but −0.54 pp, far beyond the ≤0.15 pp allowed. The committee unanimously voted refuted.

Weakened on two counts. (1) The freeze doses it relies on (E037, E053, E055) confound lost steps with a compressed anneal, so the '75% knee' is not established (N5, H2.6.6). (2) E061 removed early 20 px steps that update every still-learning layer at almost no cost, against the claim that such steps are worth the dial's rate wherever they sit. Search: a gradient-attribution layer selection ranked no better than random, which is a caution for H7.1.
Search (2603.28921): gradient-based per-layer importance failed to beat random selection. The ΔW/W curves must be validated against E028, E037 and E055 before they drive decisions.

new.statement: In the ~225-step regime, accuracy is set by per-step update and representation quality more than by step or pixel count. Changes that degrade per-step progress cost far above the dial: SGD in place of Muon −3.0 pp (E062), ReLU in place of GELU −0.54 pp (E056), stride-2 stem −1.1 pp (E051), each 3–10x worse than its time saving buys at ~0.77 s/pp. Changes that improve per-step quality (Muon hyperparameters, batch size, fitting speed) are the main untried path to the ~0.13 pp of margin the local bar needs.

Muon's hyperparameters are CIFAR-10 airbench94 copies (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, 3-ish NS steps) that were never tuned for a 225-step CIFAR-100 run with progressive resizing and freezes. E014 (lr ×1.5, +0.09 pp, 3 seeds) is the only probe. Given E062, a modest retune is the most likely near-time-neutral booster.

On the E061 tip, raising the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.8 (Nesterov kept, lr unchanged) raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds at unchanged time. It is refuted if it falls by ≥0.12 pp. Muon critical-batch theory (a lower b* at higher β) and the CIFAR-100 critical-damping result (faster early, −1.7 pp final) both predict that outcome.

The recipe under-fits CIFAR-100: at the end of training, the averaged weights' training accuracy is well below saturation. Changes that speed fitting help (E016 wd ×0.5), and changes that slow fitting or reduce capacity cost heavily (E051, E056, E062). Then regularizer additions (jitter, ghost BN, extra LS) are not worth testing. The counterpoints are E022 (wd ×0.25 hurt) and E032 (removing LS late hurt), which suggest some regularization is still useful.

Diagnostic, offline and outside the timed path: on the E061 tip (seeds 33–35), evaluate the final averaged weights on a fixed 10k training subset at 32 px with no augmentation and no LS. Prediction: train top-1 ≤90% (under-fitting). If it is ≥97%, the recipe is fitting-saturated: test LS 0.1 (H1.5.5) and jitter (H1.5.8) on 60 draws, and deprioritize the optimizer and capacity work in N1.1.

E062's −3.0 pp, with near-identical seeds (sd ~0.05 pp), is largely an SGD mis-scaling artefact, not optimizer quality: the conv lr was scaled for batch 2000 on top of the port's own airbench batch normalization, and/or the filter wd was coupled to lr 9.0. Reading commit cdfccca confirms a double scaling or coupling, and a 3-seed SGD run at lr ×0.5 recovers ≥1 pp of the gap. This is low priority unless the SGD branch is reopened; even then, closing the gap to within 0.35 pp is needed for SGD to break even.

E062's time counterexample: dropping Muon saved 0.28 s per trial, but Newton-Schulz GPU time is only ~0.18 s (0.8 ms × 226, E043). The excess ~0.1 s is per-call host and launch overhead from separate per-group Muon calls (three filter groups, each with its own schedule) plus the non-fused momentum update. Merging all Muon filter groups into one compiled, batched NS-plus-update call, with GPU-resident per-group LR tables and identical math, cuts mean time on the E061 tip by ≥1% (≥0.05 s), confirmed by per-step CUDA-event timing, with per-seed accuracies unchanged within rebuild noise. It is refuted if the per-step GPU time of the Muon section already accounts for the 0.28 s (E047's 2.8% idle bounds the overhead share).

The 75% group-1 freeze is not free; E028's '−0.01 pp' was a 10-seed reading with SE ~0.12 pp. On the E061 tip, moving the group-1 freeze, and its anneal end, from 75% to 80% of steps costs about +11 steps × 7.7 ms ≈ +0.09 s and raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds. That beats the ~0.77 s/pp dial (break-even ~0.11 pp). If it gains ≥0.15 pp, spend it on an early 20 px trim.

Freeze-dose readings are anneal-plus-freeze composites. On the E061 tip, keep group 1's LR anneal ending at 75% but move only the detach earlier, to 71% (group 1 gets ~9 more steps at a near-zero LR before the detach, then no updates). Prediction: this loses ≤0.1 pp on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds against E061, far less than E055's −0.29 pp for the same detach point, showing that most of E055's cost came from compressing the group-1 decay over ~23–71% of the run, not from the lost late steps.

Selection bias sits only in the kept tip's own recorded value and is about the size of the keep margin (~0.05 pp; E049: 0.7539 on 13–32 vs 0.7534 on fresh 33–52). Every rebuild re-draws per-seed outcomes (E057), so reused seed sets carry no persistent bias toward a tip. The ~0.2 pp deficits that challengers showed after each keep (E022, E025, E030, E032, E040–E042, E052, E053) are mostly real effects of those changes. Rule: re-measure the baseline in fresh builds rather than retiring seed sets.

Run the E061 tip (376f231) on reserved seeds 53–72 in 2 fresh builds (40 draws). Prediction: its mean lies within 0.06 pp of its 33–52 mean (0.7532). This also gives the confirmation read the H4.6 gate requires. A drop of ≥0.12 pp would revive a selection-bias account beyond the tip's recorded value.

Re-measure the post-freeze epoch dial at full power. On the E061 tip, run −0.25 and +0.25 true-epoch arms (all schedules kept as step fractions), each over 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds, against E061 on the same seeds. Prediction: the dial lies in 0.5–1.2 s/pp, and its 95% CI excludes 1.5 s/pp. This replaces E059's single 20-draw point as the exchange rate for every booster and cut.

Early-trim dose (the I099 crux shared by all four committee members). On the E061 tip, remove a further 12 steps from the 20 px phase (225 → 213), with the 28/32 px phases, whitening detach and freezes kept at the same absolute steps. This saves ~0.15 s and loses ≤0.1 pp on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds against E061. At ~0.77 s/pp the break-even loss is ~0.2 pp. It is refuted, meaning E061 used up the free early steps, if the loss is ≥0.2 pp.

Part of GELU's fused-kernel cost (E056: ReLU saved 4.8%) is erf compute, not bytes. Offline profile of the E061 32 px and 28 px steps (synthetic channels_last, batch 2000): approximate='tanh' GELU cuts per-step GPU time by ≥1.5%. If it does, the change is committed only if the mean on 60 draws stays within 0.1 pp. The search predicts ~0: tanh-GELU saves the same fp16 input and moves the same bytes. A null result closes H6.5's activation branch with no accuracy run.

structured_output.summary:
I corrected two verdicts that pointed the wrong way and dropped the seed-set bias model; the main job now is buying about 0.13 pp of accuracy margin cheaply.

**Corrected verdicts**
- **E062 (SGD in place of Muon):** it supports H1.2.2 (−3.0 pp, where the hypothesis predicted a drop of at least 0.3 pp). It had been logged as refuting it only because the experiment's own pre-registered range missed. I raised H1.2 to supported 0.6. The caveat: only one untuned SGD setup was tried, and the near-identical seeds suggest a learning-rate scaling bug (new N2).
- **E059 (epoch dial):** the measured ~0.77 s/pp sits inside H4.2.6's predicted band, so I marked it supported (0.55). H4.2 now states the dial as one number with a confidence interval of roughly 0.5–2 s/pp, because it rests on a single 20-draw build. New N7 re-measures it at 60 draws per arm.

**Seed-set bias refuted (E057)**
- Each rebuild re-draws every seed's outcome independently, and the kept tip's own value is optimistic by only ~0.05 pp. So H4.4, H4.4.3 and H4.5 are refuted, and H4.4.1 and H4.4.2 are retired. New N6 replaces them: the challenger deficits of ~0.2 pp seen after each keep are mostly real effects.
- I restored E022, E025, E030, E032 and E040 as probable real harms, and removed the hedges in H1, H1.3 and H2.3 that depended on the bias story.
- H4.1(a) now bounds the rebuild variation of a 20-seed mean at ≲0.06 pp.
- **Seed-1 recount:** I recounted from the logged per-seed numbers, over post-E049 runs only. Seed 1 is the lowest of seeds 0–2 in 9 of 15 runs, against 5 expected by chance (p≈0.03). That is suggestive, so H4.1.6 stays open at low priority. It doesn't affect the keep gate, because the seeds 0–2 average across builds matches the population mean.

**Where the tip stands (H4 and H4.6)**
- The tip is now E061: 5.02 s, with a population mean of ~0.7532 from 40 fresh draws. That passes the local 0.753 bar only about half the time per build.
- E058 showed the official 40-seed bar is easy to clear. The local bar is the binding one: a population of about 0.7545 is needed to pass it about 80% of the time.
- New rule: any keep whose effect is under 0.2 pp needs at least 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds per arm. Any time claim under 1% needs per-step CUDA-event timing.
- H2.6.11 (whitening detach at 6%) is downgraded to inconclusive: its time saving is unverified and inside build noise. A code read should also confirm that E061's commit actually carries the 6% detach.

**Counterexamples the committee didn't predict**
- **E062 time:** dropping Muon saved more than its Newton-Schulz GPU time accounts for. New N3: merging the separate Muon calls into one may recover ~0.1 s of overhead.
- **E062 accuracy:** explained by N2 (scaling) and the new Lvl1 below.
- **E056 time:** ReLU's saving fits the memory-bound account, so H6 is now supported. H6.5.1 is refuted. Search says SiLU and tanh-GELU move the same bytes as GELU, so N9 is a cheap profile-only check.
- **E046 and E031:** already explained by H6.6.
- **E043 accuracy:** rebuild noise.
- **E032:** read as a real harm under the restored H1.3.

**New Lvl1, N1 (per-step update quality):** in a ~225-step run, changes that degrade each step's progress (SGD swap, ReLU, stride-2 stem) cost 3–10× more than the dial. Its children:
- N1.1.1: Muon momentum 0.6→0.8.
- N1.2 and N1.2.1: does the recipe under-fit? A one-off train-accuracy diagnostic that decides whether the regularizer ideas are worth testing.
- H1.5.6 is re-based on E061 as a Muon lr ×1.5 test.

**Freeze tests were confounded:** every freeze-dose run moved the learning-rate anneal end along with the freeze point. H2.6 now flags this, H2.6.7 is refuted as stated, and H7 and H7.1 are lowered (E061's nearly free early trim also contradicts H7).
- N5 separates the two factors by moving only the detach point.
- N4 tests freezing *later* (80%), likely a booster better than the dial.

**Other changes**
- **Batch size (H5):** search bounds its time effect at 1–3% (E047), so it is now mainly an accuracy lever. H5.1.4 is retired, and H5.1.2 is re-based as batch 1600 on E061.
- **Lowered or retired:** H1.8 and H1.8.1 lowered (the HAF results are a strong counter-prior). H1.4 marked supported from the airbench paper. H1.3.5, H1.5.5, H1.5.8 and H1.5.9 lowered or gated behind N1.2.1. H2.5.2 and H2.3.8 retired.
- **Resolution:** H2.3.7 is re-based as moving the 28→32 px switch from 70% to 65% of steps.
- **Next trim:** N8 continues the early 20 px trim.
- **Tip check:** N6.1 confirms E061 on reserved seeds 53–72.

Lvl1 hypotheses still open: H5, H7 and N1.
